text:
Five games was as far as the Devils' winning streak would go. Winnipeg ended it and stretched its own run to four straight, and the man who did the most damage was a player New Jersey drafted. Dawson Mercer, taken 18th overall by the Devils in 2020, scored twice against his old club, including a power-play goal in the third that put the Jets ahead 3-2. Kyle Connor sealed it with an empty-net-style insurance goal at 19:02 of the third, his second of the night.

The score flatters Winnipeg's evening a little. New Jersey had 51 shot attempts to the Jets' 46, and at even strength the chances were level, 1.53 expected goals (a measure of shot quality) for NJD against 1.51 for WPG. Our simulated replays of every shot had the Devils winning 51% of the time. The Jets' edge came from special teams: they scored on two of four power plays while New Jersey went 0 for 4. Winnipeg also outhit the Devils 22-8 and took the puck away seven times to New Jersey's two. After a 1-0 and 2-0 start from Mercer and Connor, the Devils answered with two goals 44 seconds apart early in the second, from Jesper Bratt and Cody Glass, and then the game sat tied at 2 for a long stretch. Winnipeg's third period, 1.8 expected goals to 0.63, decided it.

Nico Daws stopped 19 of 21 shots, just ahead of what the chances called for. Jake Allen faced 24 and let in three, a shade below expectation. For the Devils, the streak is over, though we have no other record details beyond that. The Jets carry four wins in a row into their next game.
